entities.summary: Millard Lazare Meiss was an American art historian, one of whose specialties was Gothic architecture. Meiss worked as an art history professor at Columbia University from 1934 to 1953. After teaching at Columbia, he became a professor at Harvard until 1958, when he joined the Institute for Advanced Study, in Princeton, N.J. Meiss has edited several leading art journals and has also written articles and books on medieval and Renaissance painting. Among his many important contributions are Italian style in Catalonia and a fourteenth century Catalan workshop (1941), Painting in Florence and Siena after the Black Death (1951) and French Painting in the Time of Jean de Berry.

historicalSignificance.significanceNarrative: Meiss's work on Gothic architecture and his publications on medieval and Renaissance painting have contributed significantly to the field of art history, particularly in understanding the development of Italian style in Catalonia and the impact of the Black Death on art in Florence and Siena.
